author: codex-root

patch.value: Official Home Assistant 2026.7-era documentation and current Core dev source add searchable media sources while retaining media player search, browse, and resolve contracts. The local Core 2026.7.4 supports media player search and media source browse, but correctly reports the newer media source search command as unavailable. Deliver a typed surface that validates current media classes, bounds agent output, preserves generic passthrough, and reports server capability failures without masking them.
Add agent-native media discovery and search
Expose current Home Assistant media source and media player browse, search, and resolve WebSocket contracts through a typed, bounded, read-only CLI surface.

hassio media browse, search, and resolve expose the official WebSocket payloads with detailed recursive help and pre-network validation; Search supports media-player and media-source scopes, current media-class filters, count and positive bounded limits, stable machine-readable output, and honest unsupported-command errors; Built and installed hassio passes formatter, schema, help, isolated wizard, live read-only, package, security, release-dry-run, and PM acceptance; All source coverage and docstrings remain 100 percent, source files remain at or below 300 code lines, and no private live details enter Git or PM
Official docs, Core dev source, installed dependency contracts, all-status PM lineage, current GitHub state, and redacted live capability probes have been inspected
Agents can discover playable media and search supported providers without hand-authoring opaque WebSocket payloads.
Adds token-bounded read-only discovery for one of Home Assistant 2026.7 development cycle most relevant API additions.
A stable typed CLI contract that works on supported servers and fails transparently on older capability sets.
Home Assistant added searchable media sources in July 2026, while this CLI only offers generic WebSocket passthrough.

value.text: All-status keyword searches found no canonical media discovery or search delivery item; this feature extends rather than duplicates the closed general API parity lineage.

value.text: Never persist raw browse trees, search results, media identifiers, signed URLs, entity IDs, or local instance details. Durable evidence is limited to versions, command names, counts, booleans, and exit classifications.

value.text: Current Core dev defines media_source/search_media with media_content_id, search_query, and optional media_filter_classes; local stable 2026.7.4 does not yet register that newest command.

message: Create duplicate-safe media discovery feature from official and live research
